title: Kayaker attacked by a shark off Paradise Cove in Malibu as dramatic video emerges
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Kayaker attacked by a shark off Paradise Cove in Malibu as dramatic video emerges

A kayaker was reportedly bitten twice by a shark near Paradise Cove before a nearby fisherman and Los Angeles County lifeguards helped bring him safely to shore.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A kayaker was reportedly attacked by a shark while fishing off Malibu Sunday morning, suffering at least two bites to the lower portion of his body.

The attack happened around 8:30 a.m. near the popular cafe at Paradise Cove, according to Traffic News Los Angeles.

The victim was fishing from a kayak when a small shark reportedly bit him, causing him to fall into the water, TLNA reported.

The shark, described in preliminary reports as a possible mako, allegedly circled back and bit the man a second time.

A nearby fisherman witnessed the attack and immediately went to the victim’s aid, pulling him from the water and onto his boat.

The injured man then called his girlfriend, a retired lifeguard, who contacted 911.

Los Angeles County lifeguards responded to the scene and helped get the victim safely back to shore. He was then transported by ambulance for treatment of his injuries.

The California Post has reached out to Los Angeles County lifeguards for further information, including confirmation of the attack, the victim’s condition and whether the shark has been identified as a mako.

Officials have not yet publicly confirmed the shark species or provided additional details about the victim’s injuries.

Dramatic video from the scene shows a lifeguard rushing through the water during the rescue.

The footage appears to show calm conditions off the Malibu coastline, with a small boat nearby as the rescue unfolds.

At one point, a man can be seen swimming toward the boat, although it remains unclear whether he is the kayaker who was attacked.

The video does not appear to clearly show the shark itself, and there are no obvious signs in the footage that would independently confirm the reported attack.

The circumstances surrounding the encounter remain under investigation.

The incident comes as lifeguards and beachgoers remain on alert for marine wildlife encounters along the Southern California coast.

Sharks can venture into shallow coastal waters for several reasons, most commonly in search of food. Warmer water, concentrations of baitfish and changing tides can bring prey closer to shore, drawing sharks with them.

In Southern California, sharks can be found relatively close to the coastline throughout the year, with activity often increasing during the warmer months. Some species also use shallow coastal areasas nursery habitat, particularly when juvenile sharks are present.

Shark activity can also increase around dawn and dusk, when lower light levels and movements of prey can create favorable feeding conditions
